Parity details

The comparisons behind the overview's parity scores.

Parity (measured after determinism)

Parity compares a backend's log with ptrace's after both pass the repeatability check. The compared backends are kvm, liteinst, sabre, dbt, in-guest-trap; their test inputs must match. A full log match scores 1. Otherwise, the score is the matching start of the logs divided by the length of the longer log. Parity = matching INFO logs; partial credit = matched prefix / longer log. Parity has its own denominator: tests selected for ptrace verification, on each candidate backend. Tests without a usable ptrace log, cases with incompatible inputs, and cases omitted from a sampled run are excluded. Disabled, missing or failed candidate results score 0. These scores come from the saved parity summary, checked against its run records. Download the summary and recorded comparisons.

Newest 20 runs per host and producer, plus current headlines and pinned or retracted runs; 1,243 runs archived. Row and run counts describe this retained window.

candidate-not-enabled
The manifest does not enable the candidate's verify cell (the backend is disabled for the test, or the test has no verify mode for it), so full validation never runs it. The cell's reason carries the manifest's disabled reason.
candidate-not-selected
The candidate's verify cell is enabled, but full validation does not select it (a ci: false entry, a focused run type, an occasional test), and this run has no row for it. The cell's reason says why it is not selected.
no-result-row
The reference or the candidate has no usable result row: none in the run, a retry history hermit refuses, or a row the caller rejected as invalid.

parity-all run pressure-d44b1911e009-20261022T051816Z-parity-all

This is a parity-all run: every verify cell of every test in the parity population, on ptrace and on every candidate backend, whatever the manifests enable. A candidate the manifests disable ran as a parity probe on ptrace's guest arguments (with --max-timeslice=disabled on liteinst and in-guest-trap), not as its manifest describes it, so its credit says how far its log follows ptrace's on the same inputs; it is not evidence that the cell can be enabled.
